column3: Hebrew uses uncompleted verb forms, rendered here “I will thank” and “I will sing”; BSB uses present forms.
Hebrew says God magnified His word above all His name; BSB coordinates His name and word as exalted above all else.
Hebrew ends with the noun “strength” in the speaker’s soul; BSB expresses a second action, “strengthened my soul.”
Hebrew gives the reason, “for they have heard”; BSB has “when they hear.”
Hebrew says they sing “in the ways”; BSB says “of the ways.”
Hebrew begins “for” and says He “sees” the lowly; BSB has “though” and “attends to.”
Hebrew separates keeping the speaker alive from stretching out a hand against the foes’ anger; BSB attaches “from the anger” to preserving him.
Hebrew says the LORD will complete for the speaker without naming an object; BSB supplies “His purpose.”
